2. Operational Summary – Last 72 Hours
2A. Arabian Gulf
No confirmed attacks or disruptions were reported in this period.
Traffic flows continued, with anchorage congestion high across the region.
2B. Strait of Hormuz
Two attacks were reported in this period (UKMTO 197-26 and 200-26), against four in the previous
period. On 05 November an outbound tanker reported an explosion at the waterline, this was the
fifth attack off the Musandam coast of Oman since 01 November (UKMTO 191-26, 193-26, 194-
26, 195-26 and 197-26).
IRGC attacks, attempted attacks, and/or harassment activity persisted including UAV overflight,
targeted surveillance of merchant shipping, and occasional VHF hailing. These actions continue to
demonstrate Iran’s intent to assert presence along key transit lanes and maintain pressure on
transiting vessels.
Commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remained at reduced levels compared to the 2025
baseline. Independent tracking data indicated single to low double digit transits per day, while US
NCAGS data indicated an average of approx. 30 U.S. assisted transits per day on 05–07.
2C. Gulf of Oman
On 07 Nov UKMTO reported an incident/ blockade enforcement involving a bulk carrier and
military forces in the Gulf of Oman, approx. 18 NM east of Khor Fakkan, UAE (UKMTO 198-26).
Naval presence remained elevated due to blockade enforcement activity. According to official
CENTCOM figures issued on 07 Nov, 147 commercial vessels have been redirected and five
merchant ships have been disabled as a result of blockade enforcement. Two vessels had previously
been reported boarded for blockade compliance (CENTCOM, 01 Nov).
Vessels were expected to respond promptly to military queries and maintain AIS-on unless
constrained by security threats. Operators continued to exercise caution due to regional strike
activity and ongoing IRGC monitoring of shipping in adjacent waters.

2D. Arabian Sea (No change)
No confirmed attacks or disruptions were reported in this period. Naval forces continued routine
patrols, and commercial traffic was transiting without significant disruption.
2E. Gulf of Aden (No change)
No confirmed attacks or disruptions were reported in this period.
Commercial traffic remained relatively steady in the Gulf of Aden.
2F. Southern Red Sea & Bab el Mandeb
No confirmed attack on merchant shipping was reported in this period. On 06 Nov MSCIO reported
suspicious activity in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait (MSCIO 172/26). Traffic remains below the 20 Jul
Houthi selective embargo. Commercial traffic in the Bab el Mandeb averaged approx. 28 transits
per day on S&P tracking on 05–07 Nov, against approx. 35 per day in the previous week.
Bab el-Mandeb remains open to commercial traffic but is considered as volatile. Houthi statements
continue to assert that non-Saudi commercial shipping may transit safely. The Houthi-run
Humanitarian Operations Coordination Center (HOCC) advertises a voluntary, free ‘safe transit’
request service for vessels outside its declared ban. Recent reporting that merchant vessels have
used this service remains independently unconfirmed.
2G. Somali Coast and Somali Basin (No change)
No confirmed attacks or disruptions were reported in this period. One merchant vessel remains
hijacked since the date of initial incident reporting:

    MT ASANA, a Tanzanian-flagged product/chemical tanker, was hijacked on 17 July 2026
     approx. 65 NM southwest of Mukalla, Yemen, while carrying oil products.


2H. Northern Red Sea & Suez Canal (No change)
No confirmed attacks or disruptions were reported in this period. Maritime traffic in the Northern
Red Sea and Suez Canal held steady over the last 72 hours.
2I. Eastern Mediterranean (No change)
No confirmed attacks or disruptions were reported in this period. This is consistent with the
persistent baseline.

4. Maritime Incidents & Traffic Assessment
4A. Confirmed Vessel Incidents since 01 March

Total of 177 incidents since 01 March; five incidents since the last report (UKMTO 197-26,
MSCIO 172/26, UKMTO 198-26, UKMTO 199-26 and UKMTO 200-26). The total includes all
incidents listed in Table 1.

N.B: Correction: the total in Update 110 should have read 166, not 167; the error was a double
count. Totals from previous update, JMIC Advisory Update 111, are corrected.

4B. Infrastructure Incidents (Last 72 Hours) (No change)
The overall risk remains MODERATE, driven by the potential for an increase in kinetic activity
against ports, terminals and offshore installations along the Iranian, Yemeni and Saudi coasts.
No attack on ports, terminals, offshore platforms, oil and gas loading facilities or subsea
infrastructure was reported in this period.

4D. Port & Anchorage Congestion

Congestion remains high and is driven primarily by restricted transit, and to a lesser degree by port
capacity. On 08 Nov approx. 162 vessels were at anchor in the vicinity of Fujairah/Khor Fakkan,
approx. 144 off Dubai/Jebel Ali to Ras Al Khaimah, mainly off Sharjah/Ajman/Umm Al Quwain,
approx. 46 in the vicinity of Musandam/Sohar and approx. 32 off Bandar Abbas/Qeshm according
to internal estimates. Bandar Abbas / Qeshm counts remain low confidence because Iranian AIS
coverage is thin and the base is small; satellite imagery will be used to cross-check once all tests are
validated.
There was no mass departure, new cluster or gap near an attack area, including off Musandam
where one attack was reported; Fujairah/Khor Fakkan eased gradually (from about 179 to about 162
vessels since 05 Nov) and Musandam/Sohar fell on a small base (from about 50 to about 46), while
Dubai/Jebel Ali to Ras Al Khaimah was broadly unchanged and Bandar Abbas/Qeshm rose on a
small, low-confidence base (from about 17 to about 32). JMIC internal tracking counted approx.
208 commercial vessels stationary at the main anchorages east of the Strait of Hormuz (Fujairah,
Khor Fakkan, Sohar and Musandam), against single-digit to low double-digit AIS-visible transits
per day; thus, the backlog is expected to persist.

Data limits: internal AIS estimates; AIS-dark vessels excluded. Satellite radar imagery is consistent
with the AIS picture of vessel concentrations at the Fujairah, Khor Fakkan and Sohar anchorages.
No significant change in anchorage activity is anticipated in the next reporting period.




4E. GNSS / AIS Interference

GNSS interference in the Arabian Gulf was broadly stable on 7 Nov, at or below its weekly level;
the most consistent indications were on the Ras al-Khaimah coast at the Hormuz approaches.
Windward recorded 154 jammed vessels of 7,100 transmitting in the Gulf and Gulf of Oman on 5
Nov, about 62% below its 7-day average. UKMTO's weekly VRA report (week ending 06 Nov)
recorded three vessel GNSS reports and listed the Red Sea, Gulf of Oman and Arabian Gulf as
unchanged hotspots. In the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf of Oman, aircraft indications remained
low.
In the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb, no significant GNSS interference was observed at sea; aircraft
data showed limited indications in the southern Red Sea (single source).
No new specific UKMTO, MARAD, NAVCENT, or NAVAREA IX GNSS/EMI notices were
issued 05 – 08 November. Baseline advisories remain in force.



5. Outlook (24–48 Hours)
5A. Arabian Gulf
The threat level remains SUBSTANTIAL, with continued navigational system interference and
demonstrated kinetic threat and wider regional military activity continued to warrant caution.
Outlook: Eight attacks inside the Gulf since 07 Oct, including the 01 Nov attack on a tanker approx.
72 NM east of Ras Al Khafji (UKMTO 192-26) and the 04 Nov attack on a tanker approx. 50 NM
north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar (UKMTO 196-26), demonstrate that attacks remain a strong
possibility throughout the Arabian Gulf, including the northern and central Gulf, anchorages and
STS areas. Electronic interference remains a credible concern in the central and southern Arabian
Gulf. The operating environment requires heightened situational awareness throughout all
approaches.
Vessels stationary for extended periods, or maintaining AIS-on while static, may face elevated
targeting risk.
5B. Strait of Hormuz

The threat level remains SEVERE, with deliberate attacks considered highly likely under current
conditions.
Outlook: the 05 Nov attack on an outbound tanker approx. 16 NM east of Khasab (UKMTO 197-
26) was the fifth off the Musandam coast of Oman since 01 Nov, demonstrating that further attacks
on transiting vessels, including tankers, tugs and dhows, are highly likely, particularly off
Musandam. The 07 Nov attack on an outbound tanker in the Strait of Hormuz (UKMTO 200-26)
also indicates that the threat to transiting vessels persists.
Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is expected to remain at reduced levels, compared to
the 2025 baseline, across both the northern Iranian-controlled route and the southern Omani
corridor. Operator caution should continue, driven by a series of vessel attacks, ongoing U.S.
blockade enforcement, and elevated regional tension. Vessels transiting with AIS-on can expect
elevated targeting risk and receive directed hails instructing them to divert toward the northern
Iranian-controlled route.
The U.S. blockade of Iranian ports continues to be enforced. Unauthorized entry or departure may
result in interception or force. Neutral transit is permitted, but vessels should expect
visit-and-search checks, strong U.S. naval presence, persistent IRGC monitoring, and increased
VHF hails. A 30 NM standoff from U.S. units is advised to reduce misidentification risk.
A vetted humanitarian-cargo exemption remains in place but requires submission to NAVCENT
NCAGS. Approved vessels may transit to Iranian ports but remain subject to inspection and may
not load cargo in Iran beyond fuel and stores.
Industry Guidance for Safe Management of Vessel Transit through the Strait of Hormuz:
https://www.maritimeglobalsecurity.org/media/vkaa3pjr/2026-05-20-guidance-strait-of-hormuz.pdf

5C. Gulf of Oman
The threat level remains MODERATE. Vessels can expect persistent IRGC monitoring and routing
pressure in western portion of the Gulf of Oman; however, further east/south, attacks are considered
possible but not likely. Residual risk diminishes with distance from the primary concentration of
IRGC activity and with distance from Musandam / Jask.
Outlook: Approx. 162 vessels are at anchor in the vicinity of Fujairah/Khor Fakkan and congestion
is expected to persist. Neutral vessels between non-Iranian ports may be questioned, visited and
searched under the blockade and should be prepared to provide the documentation noted in JMIC
Advisory Note 016-26 to expedite clearance.
A U.S. naval blockade remains enforced, with ongoing monitoring, hailing, and verification
queries, particularly near approaches to Iranian ports. Unauthorized entry or departure may result in
interception or force. Neutral transit is permitted, but vessels should expect visit-and-search checks,
strong U.S. naval presence, persistent IRGC monitoring, and occasional hails. A 30 NM standoff
from U.S. units is advised, as well as ensuring continuous monitoring of VHF Channel 16, to
reduce misidentification risk.
Electronic interference continues to present a credible concern. The operating environment requires
heightened situational awareness throughout all approaches.
5D. Arabian Sea (No change)
The threat level remains MODERATE. The regional posture remains stable, with no confirmed
maritime attacks reported. Residual risk persists due to broader regional tensions; an attack is
possible but not likely, and current indicators do not suggest any shift toward increased threat levels
in the near term.



                                                                                                     7

Outlook: no attack was reported in this period; further interaction with military forces enforcing the
blockade is possible, and no change is expected.




5E. Gulf of Aden
The threat level remains SUBSTANTIAL. Attacks and piracy-related activity remain a strong
possibility in the Gulf of Aden and IRTC. Small-craft groups retain close-approach capability, and
Pirate Action Groups can still board and divert merchant vessels as monsoon restrictions are gone.
Outlook: Additional small boat approaches are likely in the western Gulf of Aden and the IRTC;
MSCIO continues to advise strict adherence to BMP-MS. The southwest monsoon subsided on 15
Oct and there is no issued storm warning for the Arabian Sea; sea state across the Gulf of Aden is
forecast to remain slight, with wave heights of approx. 0.8–1.5 m and winds of 13–18 kt through
the reporting period. These conditions permit continued skiff operations across the Gulf of Aden
and the IRTC.
5F. Southern Red Sea / Bab el Mandeb
The threat level remains SUBSTANTIAL. Houthi messaging consistently frames the 20 July
maritime blockade as selective against assets considered as Israeli-, Saudi-, or Yemeni
internationally recognized government-linked. Houthi forces retain coastal presence and strike
capability along the southern Red Sea approaches following Sept territorial gains. Saudi-backed
Yemeni government forces launched a counter-offensive in early Oct and have claimed gains in the
Bab el-Mandeb approaches; the precise extent of control remains still contested and unverified by
independent sources.
Disclosure of voyage information in response to Houthi communications (HOCC) may increase
targeting risk. U.S. MARAD Advisory 2026-013 advises U.S.-flagged commercial vessels to
disregard Houthi instructions to activate AIS or submit voyage information and to report such
contacts.
Outlook: Retaliatory action against Saudi-, Israeli- or Yemeni government-linked shipping remains
possible. Houthi long-range missile and drone capability against the waterway is assessed as
retained despite limited government gains. Attacks in the wider area remain a strong possibility but
expansion into indiscriminate targeting of all commercial shipping remains unlikely. Traffic will
continue at reduced but stable levels.
Mariners should maintain heightened security postures, implement speed and timing mitigation,
minimize predictable AIS behavior in the narrows, and prepare for short-notice navigational
directives.
5G. Somali Coast and Somali Basin
The threat level remains MODERATE as PAG activity persists across the Somali Coast and Somali
Basin. The southwest monsoon subsided on 15 Oct. Residual opportunistic piracy risk persists in
nearshore Somali waters and the Gulf of Aden, where small-boat activity remains feasible. Pirate
Action Groups retain the capability to board and divert merchant vessels along the Somali coast,
IRTC approaches, and adjacent Gulf of Aden lanes.
Outlook: the AZINI, hijacked by armed pirates off northeastern Somalia on 29 Oct and assessed by
MSCIO as a possible mother ship (UKMTO 190-26 / MSCIO 161/26), was reported liberated on 02
Nov (MSCIO 161/26 UPDATE 02), but the incident indicates that Pirate Action Group range is
likely to extend across the northern Somali Basin towards the shipping routes east and south of
Socotra; approaches to merchant vessels further offshore are a possibility. Sea state in the Somali

                                                                                                     8

Basin is forecast to remain slight, with wave heights of approx. 0.8–1.3 m and winds of 10–16 kt
throughout the reporting period, with no storm warning until next report. These conditions remain
favorable for skiff and mother-ship operations further offshore.
5H. Northern Red Sea / Suez (No change)
The threat level remains MODERATE. Periodic EMI and GNSS disruptions are likely to continue
in the area.

Outlook: Minimal AIS usage at Yanbu berths and approaches are expected to persist. The Suez
Canal will remain functional in both directions with no interruption.


5I. Eastern Mediterranean (No change)
The threat level remains LOW for security risks to merchant shipping, with localized EMI/GNSS as
the principal published hazard.
Outlook: a security incident against merchant shipping is highly unlikely, and GNSS interference
on the Levant coast will continue.
Naval presence remains, and vessels should maintain prudent separation from military units. No
change – consistent with the persistent baseline.

アデン湾西部とIRTCで小型船がさらに接近する可能性が高く、MSCIOは引き続き海事安全のベストプラクティス（BMP-MS）を厳守するよう勧告する。南西モンスーンは10月15日に弱まり、アラビア海に暴風警報は出ていない。報告対象期間のアデン湾は波高約0.8〜1.5メートル、風速13〜18ノットの穏やかな海況が続く見通し。この条件はアデン湾とIRTCでの小型船の活動継続を可能にする。

**F 紅海南部・バブエルマンデブ海峡。** 脅威水準は「相当」。フーシ派は7月20日の海上封鎖を、イスラエル、サウジアラビア、または国際的に承認されたイエメン政府と関係があるとみなす資産に対する選択的措置と説明し続ける。9月の支配域拡大を受け、紅海南部への進入路沿岸での展開と攻撃能力を維持する。サウジが支援するイエメン政府軍は10月初めに反攻を開始し、海峡進入路での前進を主張したが、支配範囲には争いがあり、独立した確認はない。

フーシ派の連絡（人道活動調整センター、HOCC）に応じて航海情報を開示すると、標的にされるリスクが高まり得る。米海事局の注意情報2026-013は、米国船籍商船に対し、AIS作動や航海情報の提出を求めるフーシ派の指示に従わず、そうした接触を報告するよう助言する。

サウジ、イスラエル、イエメン政府と関係のある船舶への報復行動は引き続きあり得る。政府側の限定的な前進にもかかわらず、フーシ派はこの水路を攻撃する長距離ミサイル・無人機の能力を維持していると評価される。広域での攻撃の可能性は強いが、すべての商船への無差別攻撃に拡大する可能性は低いとJMICはみる。通航は低水準で安定する見通し。

船舶は警戒態勢を強め、速度や通過時刻によるリスク低減策を講じ、狭窄部では予測されやすいAIS行動を減らし、直前の航行指示に備えることが望ましい。

**G ソマリア沿岸・ソマリア海盆。** 海賊集団の活動が続き、脅威水準は「中程度」。南西モンスーンは10月15日に弱まった。小型船が活動可能なソマリア沿岸付近とアデン湾では、機会を狙う海賊のリスクが残る。海賊集団にはソマリア沿岸、IRTC進入路、隣接するアデン湾航路で商船に乗り込み、針路変更を強いる能力がある。

10月29日にソマリア北東沖で武装海賊に乗っ取られ、MSCIOが母船に使われる可能性を指摘したAZINI（UKMTO 190-26／MSCIO 161/26）は、11月2日に解放されたと報告された（MSCIO 161/26 UPDATE 02）。この事案は、海賊集団の活動範囲がソマリア海盆北部を越え、ソコトラの東・南の航路に及ぶ可能性を示す。沖合の商船への接近もあり得る。ソマリア海盆の海況見通しは次頁に続く。

## PDF 9頁

**G ソマリア沿岸・ソマリア海盆の見通し（続き）。** 報告対象期間のソマリア海盆は波高約0.8〜1.3メートル、風速10〜16ノットの穏やかな海況が続く見通しで、次回報告までの暴風警報はない。小型船と母船が沖合で活動しやすい条件が続く。

ヤンブーの接岸設備と進入路ではAISの利用がごく少ない状態が続く見通し。スエズ運河は双方向で中断なく稼働する見通し。

商船の安全事案の可能性は極めて低いとJMICはみる。レバント沿岸の衛星測位への干渉は続く見通し。

### 2. 過去72時間の活動概要

**A アラビア湾。** この期間に確認済みの攻撃や航行障害は報告されなかった。通航は続き、地域全体で停泊地の混雑が続いた。

**B ホルムズ海峡。** この期間に報告された攻撃は2件（UKMTO 197-26と200-26）で、前期は4件だった。11月5日に外向きに通航するタンカーが喫水線付近の爆発を報告した。これは11月1日以降、オマーンのムサンダム沿岸沖で5件目の攻撃だった（UKMTO 191-26、193-26、194-26、195-26、197-26）。

革命防衛隊による攻撃、攻撃の試み、または妨害が続いた。無人機の上空飛行、商船を対象とする監視、散発的なVHF無線呼びかけを含む。JMICは、これらの行動は主要な航路における存在感を示し、通航船への圧力を維持しようとするイランの意図を示すと評価している。

海峡の商船通航は2025年基準を下回った。独立追跡データは日当たり一桁から十数件、米海軍のNCAGSデータは11月5〜7日の米国支援通航が日当たり平均約30回と示した。

封鎖執行により海軍の展開は引き続き増強された状態だった。米中央軍の11月7日付の公式数字によると、封鎖執行で商船147隻が針路変更を求められ、5隻が航行不能となった。以前、封鎖順守の確認のため2隻が臨検されたと報告された（米中央軍11月1日）。

船舶には軍の照会に迅速に対応し、安全上の脅威による制約がない限りAISを作動させておくことが求められた。地域での攻撃活動と近接海域での革命防衛隊の監視を受け、船舶運航者は引き続き警戒した。

visit-and-search checks, strong U.S. naval presence, persistent IRGC monitoring, and increased
VHF hails. A 30 NM standoff from U.S. units is advised to reduce misidentification risk.
A vetted humanitarian-cargo exemption remains in place but requires submission to NAVCENT
NCAGS. Approved vessels may transit to Iranian ports but remain subject to inspection and may
not load cargo in Iran beyond fuel and stores.
Industry Guidance for Safe Management of Vessel Transit through the Strait of Hormuz:
https://www.maritimeglobalsecurity.org/media/vkaa3pjr/2026-05-20-guidance-strait-of-hormuz.pdf

5C. Gulf of Oman
The threat level remains MODERATE. Vessels can expect persistent IRGC monitoring and routing
pressure in western portion of the Gulf of Oman; however, further east/south, attacks are considered
possible but not likely. Residual risk diminishes with distance from the primary concentration of
IRGC activity and with distance from Musandam / Jask.
Outlook: Approx. 162 vessels are at anchor in the vicinity of Fujairah/Khor Fakkan and congestion
is expected to persist. Neutral vessels between non-Iranian ports may be questioned, visited and
searched under the blockade and should be prepared to provide the documentation noted in JMIC
Advisory Note 016-26 to expedite clearance.
A U.S. naval blockade remains enforced, with ongoing monitoring, hailing, and verification
queries, particularly near approaches to Iranian ports. Unauthorized entry or departure may result in
interception or force. Neutral transit is permitted, but vessels should expect visit-and-search checks,
strong U.S. naval presence, persistent IRGC monitoring, and occasional hails. A 30 NM standoff
from U.S. units is advised, as well as ensuring continuous monitoring of VHF Channel 16, to
reduce misidentification risk.
Electronic interference continues to present a credible concern. The operating environment requires
heightened situational awareness throughout all approaches.
5D. Arabian Sea (No change)
The threat level remains MODERATE. The regional posture remains stable, with no confirmed
maritime attacks reported. Residual risk persists due to broader regional tensions; an attack is
possible but not likely, and current indicators do not suggest any shift toward increased threat levels
in the near term.

**B ホルムズ海峡（続き）。** 脅威水準は「深刻」のまま。現在の条件では意図的な攻撃の可能性が高いとJMICは評価する。

11月5日のハサブ東方約16海里での外向きタンカーへの攻撃（UKMTO 197-26）は、11月1日以降のオマーン・ムサンダム沿岸沖で5件目だった。特にムサンダム沖で、タンカー、タグボート、ダウ船などの通航船へのさらなる攻撃の可能性が高いとJMICはみる。11月7日のホルムズ海峡の外向きタンカーへの攻撃（UKMTO 200-26）も、通航船への脅威が続いていることを示す。

2025年の基準に比べ、海峡の海上交通はイランが管理する北側航路でもオマーン側の南側回廊でも低水準が続く見通し。一連の船舶攻撃、米国による封鎖の継続、地域の緊張を踏まえ、運航者は警戒を続ける必要がある。AISを作動させて通航する船は、標的にされるリスクの上昇や、北側のイラン管理航路へ針路変更するよう個別に無線で指示されることを想定する。

米国によるイラン港湾の封鎖は引き続き執行されている。無許可で入港・出港すると、阻止や武力行使を受け得る。中立船の通航は認められるが、臨検、米海軍の強い展開、革命防衛隊の監視、VHF無線呼びかけの増加を想定する。誤認を減らすため米軍部隊から30海里離れることを勧める。

審査付きの人道支援貨物の例外措置は継続しており、NAVCENT NCAGSへの申請が必要。承認された船はイラン港へ航行できるが検査の対象であり、イランでは燃料・船用品以外の貨物を積めない。

[ホルムズ海峡の安全通航に関する業界ガイダンス](https://www.maritimeglobalsecurity.org/media/vkaa3pjr/2026-05-20-guidance-strait-of-hormuz.pdf)

**C オマーン湾。** 脅威水準は「中程度」。西部では革命防衛隊の監視・航路への圧力が続くと見込む。さらに東・南では攻撃があり得るものの可能性は高くない。革命防衛隊活動の集中域やムサンダム・ジャスクから離れるにつれ残存リスクは下がる。

フジャイラ／ホールファッカーン付近には約162隻が停泊し、混雑は続く見通し。イラン以外の港同士を移動する中立船も、封鎖の下で照会・臨検を受ける場合がある。手続を早めるためJMIC注意情報016-26に記載の書類を提示できるようにする。

米国の海上封鎖は執行中で、特にイラン港への進入路付近で監視、無線呼びかけ、確認照会が続く。無許可の入港・出港は阻止や武力行使を受け得る。中立船の通航は認められるが、臨検、米海軍の強い展開、革命防衛隊の継続監視、散発的な無線呼びかけを想定する。誤認防止のため米軍部隊から30海里離れ、VHF16チャンネルを継続監視するよう勧める。

電子的干渉は引き続き懸念される。すべての進入路で高い状況認識が求められる。

**D アラビア海（変化なし）。** 脅威水準は「中程度」。地域の状況は安定し、確認済みの海上攻撃は報告されていない。広域の緊張で残存リスクがあり、攻撃はあり得るが可能性は高くない。現時点の指標は近いうちに脅威水準が上がることを示していない。

The threat level remains SUBSTANTIAL. Attacks and piracy-related activity remain a strong

and the IRTC.
5F. Southern Red Sea / Bab el Mandeb
The threat level remains SUBSTANTIAL. Houthi messaging consistently frames the 20 July
maritime blockade as selective against assets considered as Israeli-, Saudi-, or Yemeni

**D アラビア海の見通し（続き）。** この期間の攻撃報告はない。封鎖を執行する軍部隊とのさらなる接触はあり得る。状況の変化は見込まない。

**E アデン湾。** 脅威水準は「相当」。アデン湾と国際推奨通航回廊（IRTC）では攻撃と海賊関連活動の可能性が強い。小型船の集団は接近能力を維持し、モンスーンによる制約がなくなったため、海賊集団は引き続き商船への乗り込みや針路変更の強要が可能。

アデン湾西部とIRTCで小型船がさらに接近する可能性が高く、MSCIOは引き続き海事安全のベストプラクティス（BMP-MS）を厳守するよう勧告する。南西モンスーンは10月15日に弱まり、アラビア海に暴風警報は出ていない。報告対象期間のアデン湾は波高約0.8〜1.5メートル、風速13〜18ノットの穏やかな海況が続く見通し。この条件はアデン湾とIRTCでの小型船の活動継続を可能にする。

**F 紅海南部・バブエルマンデブ海峡。** 脅威水準は「相当」。フーシ派は7月20日の海上封鎖を、イスラエル、サウジアラビア、または国際的に承認されたイエメン政府と関係があるとみなす資産に対する選択的措置と説明し続ける。9月の支配域拡大を受け、紅海南部への進入路沿岸での展開と攻撃能力を維持する。サウジが支援するイエメン政府軍は10月初めに反攻を開始し、海峡進入路での前進を主張したが、支配範囲には争いがあり、独立した確認はない。

フーシ派の連絡（人道活動調整センター、HOCC）に応じて航海情報を開示すると、標的にされるリスクが高まり得る。米海事局の注意情報2026-013は、米国船籍商船に対し、AIS作動や航海情報の提出を求めるフーシ派の指示に従わず、そうした接触を報告するよう助言する。

サウジ、イスラエル、イエメン政府と関係のある船舶への報復行動は引き続きあり得る。政府側の限定的な前進にもかかわらず、フーシ派はこの水路を攻撃する長距離ミサイル・無人機の能力を維持していると評価される。広域での攻撃の可能性は強いが、すべての商船への無差別攻撃に拡大する可能性は低いとJMICはみる。通航は低水準で安定する見通し。

船舶は警戒態勢を強め、速度や通過時刻によるリスク低減策を講じ、狭窄部では予測されやすいAIS行動を減らし、直前の航行指示に備えることが望ましい。

**G ソマリア沿岸・ソマリア海盆。** 海賊集団の活動が続き、脅威水準は「中程度」。南西モンスーンは10月15日に弱まった。小型船が活動可能なソマリア沿岸付近とアデン湾では、機会を狙う海賊のリスクが残る。海賊集団にはソマリア沿岸、IRTC進入路、隣接するアデン湾航路で商船に乗り込み、針路変更を強いる能力がある。

10月29日にソマリア北東沖で武装海賊に乗っ取られ、MSCIOが母船に使われる可能性を指摘したAZINI（UKMTO 190-26／MSCIO 161/26）は、11月2日に解放されたと報告された（MSCIO 161/26 UPDATE 02）。この事案は、海賊集団の活動範囲がソマリア海盆北部を越え、ソコトラの東・南の航路に及ぶ可能性を示す。沖合の商船への接近もあり得る。ソマリア海盆の海況見通しは次頁に続く。
